title: Ex 3.5 #19 · Counting flushes
prompt: A 5-card poker hand is a set of 5 cards from a standard 52-card deck (13 cards in each of 4 suits); the order of the cards doesn't matter. A hand is a flush if all 5 cards are of the same suit. How many different flushes are there?
answer_format: A whole number, or an expression for it like 26^4 or binom(10, 3).

mistakes.hint: That counts the flushes in one particular suit. There are four suits to choose from.
A hand is a set of cards: the order in which they are dealt doesn't matter.
That counts every 5-card hand, not just the flushes.

hints: First choose the suit, then choose which 5 of that suit's 13 cards are in the hand.
solution: Choose the suit: 4 ways. Choose 5 of its 13 cards: $\binom{13}{5} = 1287$ ways.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses combinations (Section 3.5).
